summary: Today’s edition retains the Ukraine Starlink report and adds Kim Jong Un’s reported arrival in China via the new Dandong bridge. Canada tariff relief is covered in Markets; other single-source or unconfirmed reports are held out, leaving this edition below ten stories.

stories.headline: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
stories.dek: Kyiv says restrictions on Starlink access remain in place despite President Donald Trump’s assurance that limits had been lifted.
tldr: Ukraine said Starlink restrictions remain in place after Donald Trump said the limits had been lifted, according to BBC and Reuters reporting.
The reports describe a disagreement between the public assurance and Kyiv’s account of current access.
The cited coverage does not establish the precise scope of restrictions or a timeline for any change.

body.text: Ukraine said restrictions on Starlink access remained in place after U.S. President Donald Trump said limits had been lifted. BBC reported Kyiv’s account on October 23, and Reuters separately reported that Ukraine said speed curbs remained despite Trump’s assurance.

The central confirmed point in both reports is the mismatch between the assurance and the Ukrainian account. The coverage attributes the claim about continued restrictions to Ukraine; it does not independently document the network settings in use.

The distinction matters because the reports concern access and service limits, rather than a newly announced agreement or a verified restoration. Neither cited account supplies a complete technical description of the restrictions.
The reports leave open which terminals or areas are affected, what conditions govern access, and whether the limits will change. Those details cannot be resolved from the cited reporting.

stories.whyItMatters: Starlink access has become part of the operational and diplomatic environment around Ukraine. The immediate story is the gap between Washington’s public statement and Kyiv’s description; the available reports leave the technical and policy details unsettled.
stories.editorNote: Compared BBC and Reuters coverage. The reported continued limits are attributed to Ukraine; specific network status and scope are not independently verified in the cited stories.

stories.headline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visits China, South Korean news agency reports
stories.dek: South Korean media and officials said Kim entered China via the newly opened Dandong bridge; the visit’s timing and purpose remain partly unclear.
tldr: Kim Jong Un arrived in China’s border city of Dandong by crossing a newly opened bridge, according to South Korean officials and Yonhap.
Reuters and AP also carried the report, attributing the information to South Korean sources.
The reports do not establish the visit’s full itinerary or confirm a meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

body.text: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong via a newly opened bridge linking the two countries, according to a South Korean government source cited by Yonhap. AP reported that South Korea’s Unification Ministry also said Kim appeared to have arrived in Dandong.

Reuters reported the crossing on Saturday, citing Yonhap and a South Korean government official. The bridge is the New Yalu River crossing, which the Guardian described as having opened to traffic on 15 October after a long delay.

The trip places Kim in China ahead of the 25 October anniversary of Chinese forces entering the Korean War in 1950, a timing noted by AP. His last known China visit was in September 2025, when he attended the 80th anniversary Victory Day events in Beijing, according to the same report.

The available reporting does not establish Kim’s full schedule, whether he will meet President Xi Jinping, or what agreements may be discussed. The arrival was reported through South Korean government and media sources; public confirmation from Pyongyang or Beijing was not cited in these accounts.

stories.whyItMatters: The crossing gives the newly opened land bridge immediate diplomatic visibility as Pyongyang balances ties with Beijing and Moscow. The visit’s significance will depend on whether official meetings or concrete agreements follow; those details were not confirmed in the reports available.
stories.editorNote: Arrival details are attributed to Yonhap and South Korean government sources in AP and Reuters coverage; itinerary and meeting claims remain unconfirmed.
